blocks.content: When one microservice needs to talk to another within the same cluster, it does so exactly the way covered throughout the Services module, by DNS name, resolving to a stable virtual IP that kube-proxy routes correctly, regardless of where the actual Pods live.
A Pod behind Service A reaching Service B does so the standard way, by its DNS name, exactly the naming scheme covered in the DNS topic, service-b or service-b.namespace, not a hardcoded IP.

blocks.alt: A DNS name, not a hardcoded, brittle IP address

blocks.content:
# From inside a Pod behind Service A
curl http://service-b/api/data

blocks.content: 2. Resolving to Service B's Virtual IP
blocks.text: 2. Resolving to Service B's Virtual IP

blocks.content: That DNS lookup resolves to Service B's own stable virtual IP, exactly the same lookup mechanism covered in the DNS topic, served by CoreDNS, covered later in this module.

blocks.alt: A name resolved into a stable, familiar virtual IP address

blocks.content: From that point forward, everything is exactly the Pod-to-Service mechanism covered in the previous topic, kube-proxy intercepts traffic to that virtual IP and routes it to a real, current backing Pod, no different just because the caller happens to be another Service's Pod.

blocks.alt: The exact same routing mechanism, whether the caller is a Service or not

blocks.content: 4. Independent of Which Nodes Are Actually Involved
blocks.text: 4. Independent of Which Nodes Are Actually Involved

blocks.content: This works identically no matter which physical nodes Service A's and Service B's Pods actually happen to be running on, exactly the cross-node reachability covered in the Pod-to-Pod Communication topic, made concrete for real service-to-service traffic.

blocks.alt: The physical topology underneath is entirely irrelevant to how this works

blocks.content: This is, in practice, exactly how every microservice within a Kubernetes cluster talks to every other one, a DNS name, resolved to a stable virtual IP, transparently routed to real Pods, no special configuration needed beyond the Service objects themselves.

blocks.alt: The everyday, standard pattern behind virtually all in-cluster microservice communication

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Service-to-service communication is a Pod reaching another Service by DNS name, resolved to a stable virtual IP, then routed exactly the same way as any Pod-to-Service traffic.
This works identically regardless of which physical nodes are actually involved, it is the standard, default pattern for how microservices talk to each other in a cluster.
